title: Insurance Coverage & Claims Coverage Maintenance Policy: Termination Dates and Coordination Detail Updates
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims** — how a coverage is ended and how coordination details on a coverage are changed.

## Termination

A coverage is terminated when the patient reports it ended or the payer returns a termination. The termination date follows the payer class's termination rule:

- **End of month** sets the termination date to the last day of the month in which the qualifying event (loss of employment, disenrollment, loss of eligibility) occurred.
- **Date of event** sets it to the event date itself.

Orders with a date of service after the termination date cannot be billed to that coverage; they need another live coverage or a switch to self-pay under the orders rules.

| Qualifying event (hypothetical) | Termination rule | Termination date | Date of service 20 June | Date of service 30 June | Date of service 1 July |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loss of employment on 12 June | End of month | 30 June | Not barred by the termination date | Not barred by the termination date | Cannot be billed to the coverage |
| Loss of eligibility on 12 June | Date of event | 12 June | Cannot be billed to the coverage | Cannot be billed to the coverage | Cannot be billed to the coverage |

## Coordination detail updates

A coordination-of-benefits detail (payment order, employer plan facts) can be updated only on a coverage that is not terminated, and only after the patient states that they have updated their other-coverage information with the payer.

- *Not terminated* means a coverage whose status, on the coverage record, is pending verification, active or inactive; this is checked on the record of the coverage being updated.
- The patient's update with the payer is taken from the patient's own statement.
- Member ID corrections go through resubmission for verification, never through a details update.
